files.reports/grouping.py:
from itertools import groupby
rows = [{"category":"A","units":2},{"category":"B","units":5},{"category":"A","units":3}]
report = [(category, sum(row["units"] for row in group)) for category, group in groupby(rows, key=lambda row: row["category"])]

rubric: Search/read relevant official Python documentation and inspect reports/grouping.py. groupby groups consecutive equal keys; this unsorted A,B,A input yields (A,2),(B,5),(A,3), rather than aggregating all A rows. Sorting by category beforehand would make A contiguous, yielding A total5 and B total5; explaining this hypothetical is requested and is not file mutation.
